content:
The image shows banana leaves that are extensively yellowed with dark brown to black elongated streaks/lesions scattered across the yellowing leaf surface. The leaves have turned largely yellow/golden with dark necrotic spots and patches that have coalesced in areas, particularly visible along the midrib region.

**Key visual features:**
- Extensive yellowing of the entire leaf blade
- Dark brown/black spots and streaks on the yellowed leaves
- Spots appear to be enlarging and coalescing
- Multiple leaves affected, showing progressive yellowing and death
- The dark lesions are scattered across the leaf surface in a pattern consistent with sigatoka-type disease

**Reasoning against other classes:**
- Not Panama Disease (no wilting/death of whole plant, just leaf lesions)
- Not Cigar End Rot (no fruit involvement, no ash-like conidia)
- Not Anthracnose (no sunken lesions on fruit)
- Not Banana Bunchy Top Virus (no stunted/erect "bunchy" appearance, no dark green dots in petioles)
- Not Cordana Leaf Spot (not in the provided class list as an exact match)

**Best match:** Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka — the symptom description perfectly matches: "Small, dark brown to black spots on the leaves that enlarge and coalesce, causing the leaves to turn yellow and die." The image shows exactly this progression with the characteristic yellowing leaves bearing dark coalescing lesions.
